reason: The passage attributes the suffering and burdens (סִבְלֹתָם) of the Hebrew people directly to Egyptian oppression—specifically an Egyptian (מִצְרִי) striking a Hebrew (עִבְרִי). The text does not discuss or implicate Hebrew leaders as responsible for the people's state. Instead, it portrays the source of their affliction as external (Egyptian oppression under Pharaoh), and Moses—presented as a potential leader figure—is shown sympathizing with and acting to defend his people against their oppressor, not being blamed for their condition.
